ranked.headline: Graph and generative models couple spatial omics with scRNA-seq reference structure
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications apply graph, attention, and diffusion models to integrate spatial multi-omics with single-cell references.

ranked.headline: Neural models convert spatial and histology images into cell-level molecular readouts
ranked.summary: Recent 2026 items extend graph, implicit neural and state-space models to spatial transcriptomics resolution and cell-level annotation.

ranked.headline: Deep models infer functional consequences of biological sequence variation
ranked.summary: Pretrained and deep sequence models now span DNA, RNA, protein, and CRISPR tasks, with benchmarks testing whether pretraining and architecture choices actually…

ranked.headline: Methods integrate multi-omics layers to resolve cell states and pathway programs
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications apply stability testing, Bayesian tuning and confounder adjustment to make multi-omics inference more reproducible.

ranked.headline: Protein language and structure embeddings drive functional site prediction models
ranked.summary: Recent work pairs protein language model embeddings with graph and equivariant networks to predict binding and metal-binding sites across partner types.

ranked.headline: Machine learning for omics prediction, biomarker discovery and proteomic translation
ranked.summary: Small-sample, high-dimensional omics data are pushing model design toward uncertainty calibration, graph regularization and multi-omics fusion.

ranked.headline: Multimodal fusion of molecular, structural and omics inputs for drug prediction
ranked.summary: Recent work combines structure, sequence, graph, and transcriptomic inputs to improve predictive drug discovery tasks.

ranked.headline: Protein language models predicting TCR, pMHC, and antibody-antigen recognition
ranked.summary: Recent items pair protein language model embeddings with structure, splits and weak supervision to address evaluation and label scarcity in immune prediction.

ranked.headline: MD ensembles resolve GPCR activation transitions and ligand selectivity energetics
ranked.summary: Coevolution-derived collective variables and MD ensembles now quantify transitions, binding energetics, and ligand discrimination.

ranked.headline: Microbiome tools pair error control with benchmarked validation of inferred outputs
ranked.summary: Recent tools benchmark or diagnose inferred outputs in microbiome and metagenomic analyses, from taxonomic profiling to transmission SNP thresholds.

ranked.headline: Read-based inference of variants, copy number and modifications from sequencing data
ranked.summary: Biobank-scale WGS and long-read platforms now require accurate calling of rare, paralogous, and immune-receptor loci from routine sequencing data.

ranked.headline: Allele-level methylation and mosaic Y loss estimated from read-level sequencing data
ranked.summary: Phasing-free tools now extract allele-specific methylation and chromosome Y mosaicism directly from existing read-level sequencing outputs.

ranked.headline: Priors and cell context are constraining gene regulatory network inference
ranked.summary: Single-cell and spatial multi-omics now enable gene regulatory networks resolved by cell type, trajectory, and location, with explicit regulatory priors.

ranked.headline: Task-specific priors and fusion mechanisms reshape biological representation learning
ranked.summary: Recent studies test whether learned biological representations transfer across perturbation, graph, sequence and temporal tasks.

ranked.headline: Deep sequence models and Hi-C context refine regulatory variant prioritization
ranked.summary: Recent 2026 methods combine LD-grouped deep sequence training, phylogenetic graph models and 3D genome contacts to prioritize regulatory variants.

ranked.headline: Error-aware sequencing and transcript definitions refine variant and RNA measurement
ranked.summary: Donor-specific assemblies and updatable transcript annotations now allow sequencing errors and transcript boundaries to be measured directly.

ranked.headline: Fragment-level energy attribution and structure-conditioned models target ligand binding
ranked.summary: Retrospective FEP+ validation on 230+ macrocyclic analogues and FragScan's per-fragment energy attribution target affinity optimization for drug discovery.

ranked.headline: Genome-scale metabolic models built and interrogated for microbes and communities
ranked.summary: Reconstruction tools now extend constraint-based analysis from single organisms toward community-level and functional questions.

ranked.headline: Purpose-built metrics quantify structural architecture and geometric comparison
ranked.summary: Purpose-built metrics for architectural complexity and geometric comparison are appearing across proteomes, capsids, and ribosome structures.

ranked.headline: LLMs and literature mining assign mechanistic and clinical context to human genes at scale
ranked.summary: Language-model pipelines over literature now yield gene-level annotation resources and context-aware enrichment analysis, extending beyond manual curation.

ranked.headline: Explicit cell-cycle structure is being modeled in single-cell drug response inference
ranked.summary: Curated SciPlex3 benchmarks and consensus-labeled scRNA-seq now test cell-cycle phase prediction directly within perturbation modeling workflows.

ranked.headline: Reference genome assemblies for non-model taxa from long-read and Hi-C data
ranked.summary: Long-read and Hi-C assemblies now extend reference genomes to parasites, crustaceans, protists, and fish for comparative and applied use.

ranked.headline: Molecular clocks estimate biological age from transcript damage and CpG methylation
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and papers add transcriptomic damage readouts and interpretable epigenetic clock models linking CpGs to transcription factor binding.

ranked.headline: Benchmarks and reproducible pipelines reshape genomic sequence analysis tooling
ranked.summary: Recent work pairs new read-mapping and simulation methods with benchmarks showing that tool choice changes detection outcomes in sequencing analysis.

ranked.headline: Compressed k-mer and index structures cut memory for pangenome sequence analysis
ranked.summary: Pangenome-scale sequence collections push k-mer dictionaries, LCP arrays, and graph enumeration toward compressed representations.

ranked.headline: Transformer and gradient-boosted models infer miRNA-mRNA and RNA-protein binding
ranked.summary: Sequence-based learning is now applied across RNA regulation, ribosome occupancy, 5' UTR design, and nucleic-acid-binding protein specificity.

ranked.headline: Locus-resolved genome and regulatory maps reach haplotype and structural-variant scale
ranked.summary: Gap-free assemblies, long-read haplotype profiling and cross-species atlases now resolve variation at centromere, telomere and regulatory-element scale.

ranked.headline: Benchmark construction and data splitting determine generalization in biomolecular ML
ranked.summary: Recent benchmarks in biomolecular ML test whether reported performance holds under stricter evaluation of splits, datasets and active-learning designs.

ranked.headline: Computational models infer regulatory states from indirect and sparse biological inputs
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and papers apply AlphaGenome scoring, multimodal fusion, and agent-based simulation to regulatory and immune questions from indirect data.

ranked.headline: Learned models move protein structure prediction toward ensembles and dynamics
ranked.summary: Recent work couples deep learning with experimental data and physical priors to model conformational ensembles and protein dynamics.

ranked.headline: Ensemble and base-pair-aware methods are reshaping RNA structure prediction and design
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and publications move RNA modeling from single predicted folds toward ensembles, alternative folds, and 3D generative sampling.

ranked.headline: Lineage tracing and trajectory inference reconstruct single-cell dynamics in tissue
ranked.summary: Lineage recording now coincides with spatial sampling in one tissue, while new methods infer trajectories from time-series spatial and single-cell data.

ranked.headline: Generative models constrain enzyme, rhodopsin and antimicrobial peptide design
ranked.summary: Generative and machine-learning pipelines now condition molecular design on function, light response and pathogen context, not post hoc assessment.

ranked.headline: New tools for simulating and visualizing ancestral recombination graphs
ranked.summary: Recent tools extend ancestral recombination graph simulation and visualization to biobank-scale datasets.

ranked.headline: Open-source tools unify conversion, viewing, and plotting of biomedical data
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and papers release open-source tools for proprietary imaging formats, spatial proteomics viewing, and publication-grade biomedical figures.

ranked.headline: Multiscale simulations probe nanobody inhibition and protein condensate assembly
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and papers add scalable tools for building and simulating protein systems across multiple resolutions and force fields.

ranked.headline: Transformer and foundation models are reshaping tandem mass spectrometry interpretation
ranked.summary: Transformer and foundation models now span spectrum prediction, peptide search, lipid annotation and metabolomics pipelines in recent work.

ranked.headline: Parametric and spatial models infer cell growth, size and senescence from measured data
ranked.summary: Explicit parametric and spatial models now link growth, gene expression and tissue organization to cell-level phenotypes.

ranked.headline: Duplication and pseudogene dynamics shape vertebrate and arthropod genome evolution
ranked.summary: Multi-species genome assemblies now allow duplication and pseudogene dynamics to be compared across vertebrates and other animals.

ranked.headline: Auditing error and prior bias in deep learning de novo peptide sequencing
ranked.summary: Deep learning de novo predictions need explicit bias and FDR measurement before their peptide assignments can be trusted.
